clue.text: Left-and that's ominous

definitions.meaning: on the left-hand side, the heraldic sense from Latin for left

explanation.surface: A remark that leftward means something bad is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for the left side became an English adjective, kept in heraldry for left and in everyday use for threatening.

clue.text: The good man holds a boss of the underworld to be a vicious guy

indicators.note: the good man holds the other pieces inside him

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man
Dis is the Roman god ruling the underworld

explanation.surface: A good man protects a gangland chief who turns out to be brutal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss of the underworld' suggests a crime lord; it is Dis, Roman ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist delights in inflicting pain, the very picture of cruelty.

clue.text: Fruit with brown interior hanging down

indicators.note: the brown colour forms the inside of the fruit

parts.note: a nut is a fruit
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: A nut with a brown inside dangling from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A botanical word for nodding or drooping.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutant is the botanist's word for drooping or nodding, as a flower head does.

clue.text: Boy-one accompanying a girl

parts.note: a son is a boy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lad and a lass go out together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanying' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonia is a female first name.

clue.text: Possibly ten take a drink and wind up together

indicators.note: possibly signals the word may be another arrangement of its letters

parts.note: wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Ten people have a drink and end up tangled together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TEN into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine things is to twist or wind them around each other.

clue.text: Getting through can be so tedious

explanation.surface: Drilling through a wall can be a dull job.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is the tool for getting through material, and a dull, wearisome thing is also described by the same adjective.

clue.text: Ring a churchman up, then send round cash to appear lavish

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the churchman is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend, a churchman

indicators.note: the word send goes round the cash

parts.note: p is a penny, the smallest cash

explanation.surface: Phone a vicar, then pass money around to look generous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring a churchman' sounds like phoning a vicar; the ring is the letter O, and 'up' reads the churchman bottom to top in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend beyond one's means, often to look rich, is extravagance.

clue.text: Making a break in travel

indicators.note: making, as in remaking, indicates the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Stopping for a rest on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' rearranges IN TRAVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause or break, such as between acts of a play.

clue.text: A down-to earth individual looking for growth

definitions.text: A down-to earth individual looking for growth

parts.words: A down-to earth individual looking for growth
parts.note: not a sensible career person but someone who tends soil and hopes plants grow

explanation.surface: A practical person eager for advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tends plants works with soil and hopes for things to come up from the ground.

clue.text: Let off school in time

indicators.note: the word in places the school inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil is released from school on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' looks like a release from lessons, but it means to set off an explosive. ETON is the English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off a bomb or firework is to set off its explosion.

clue.text: The character of a person's correspondence?

definitions.meaning: a written message sent by post

explanation.surface: A query about what a person's letters reveal of their nature.
explanation.definitionFit: The same noun names an alphabet symbol and a written message posted to someone.

clue.text: Split photograph

definitions.meaning: to break suddenly with a crack

explanation.surface: A torn picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to break with a crack, and the noun is a quick snapshot photo.

clue.text: Feeling no inset's a mistake

indicators.note: a mistake here means the letters are put in a wrong, jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
the word inset with its S, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone senses that leaving out an inset was an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' rearranges the nine letters of NO INSETS A.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is a physical feeling perceived through the senses.

clue.text: eg Reserve backing material

indicators.note: backing says the pieces in front of it are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Res is the standard abbreviation for reserve; that the full letters also sit in the clue is a coincidence of the abbreviation, not a hidden run

explanation.surface: A note about something like a reserve fabric being supported.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals a hidden run, so this is not one: 'backing' turns EG plus RES (reserve) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen fabric, used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Away the old-fashioned make personal complaint

parts.note: read as 'a way', a street, which is abbreviated St
ye is the archaic form of the

explanation.surface: An instruction to make something out of the way into a private grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away' looks like absent, but split it as 'a way': a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an ailment of one's own body.

clue.text: Skin specialists work here-work in earnest

indicators.note: work means the letters are worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Dermatologists do their job seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skin specialists' suggests doctors, but they are leather workers treating hides. 'work' rearranges IN EARNEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanneries are workshops where hides are cured into leather.

clue.text: Quietly serving men shave and get ready

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
RE, the Royal Engineers, are men serving in the British Army
to pare is to shave off a thin layer

explanation.surface: Discreet servants give a shave and make things ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving men' sounds like valets, but it means soldiers in service: the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare is to make ready or get set in advance.

clue.text: Flattered a failure without money and made a meal

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the failure goes round the rest

parts.note: a dud is a failure
L is the pound sign, standing for money
ate means made a meal

explanation.surface: A broke failure was praised and then had dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so DUD surrounds L and ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate someone is to praise them excessively, as a flatterer does.

clue.text: A ne'er-do-well

parts.note: read literally as one who never does good, a person whose deeds are wicked

explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, someone who never does good, is a wicked person.

clue.text: Apprehends ecclesiastics

explanation.surface: A churchman is arrested, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to grasp by intuition, and the plural noun is an old word for clergymen and theologians.

clue.text: Bearing on wood that's just for decoration

parts.note: S is south, a compass bearing
ash is a wood

explanation.surface: A heading on timber that is purely ornamental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces; 'that's just for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a decorative band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: The party's a little over-scrupulous-idealistic even

indicators.note: only a little of the long phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A political group described as somewhat fussy and even idealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of 'scrupulous' and takes the first three of 'idealistic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team or party in a contest or dispute.

clue.text: Trying to find and interview a top man

parts.note: to see someone is to interview them
a king is the top man of a realm

explanation.surface: Searching for a chance to interview a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking is searching for something.

clue.text: Jack's water-spaniel?

parts.note: Jack is a sailor, so his dog would be a dog of the sea, the phrase for an old salt

explanation.definitionFit: An old, experienced sailor is nicknamed with this phrase.

clue.text: He'll finish off for the sleepyhead going to bed

parts.note: the head of sleepy is its first letter
a layer is a bed, as of rock

explanation.surface: Someone will polish off a drowsy person heading for bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleepyhead' looks like a drowsy person but gives the head of sleepy, S; 'going to' joins it to LAYER.
explanation.definitionFit: A slayer kills, finishing off his victims.

clue.text: A story told about a couple of trainees in France

indicators.note: the story goes about, around, the trainees

parts.note: a lie is a false story
L is a learner driver, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A fib told about two apprentices on a trip in France.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large city in northern France, close to the Belgian border.

clue.text: Rate highly as a flowering plant

parts.note: speed is a rate of movement
well means highly, as in thought well of

explanation.surface: To think highly of something as a blooming plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate highly' reads as one verb meaning esteem, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small herb with blue flowers, of the genus Veronica.

clue.text: Discourage the use of some trade terms

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advising against using certain business jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes the run across 'trade terms'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to put off or dissuade from doing something.

clue.text: Deceived over relations

parts.note: too means over, excessively
kin are one's family relations

explanation.surface: Someone was fooled about their family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'about', but it means excessively, TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken in is to be fooled or duped.

clue.text: An age-old celebration!

parts.note: not an ancient festival but a party marking the age one has reached, one year older

explanation.surface: A feast that has been held since time immemorial.
explanation.definitionFit: The anniversary of one's arrival in the world is celebrated as one grows a year older.

clue.text: Oppression appears quite acceptable in the outfit

indicators.note: the acceptable letter goes in the word for outfit

parts.note: a dress is an outfit
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Being oppressed seems perfectly fine when you are in a nice outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class, socially acceptable, comes from 1950s British talk of U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is compulsion by threats or force, a form of oppression.

clue.text: A fish-a fish found in sea-weed

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
the gar again

explanation.surface: One fish and then another are found among seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a jelly made from red seaweed, and the name is also used for the algae.
